expected_prisoner.name: Jim Albertini
expected_prisoner.description:
Hawaii anti-nuclear and anti-militarism activist, founder of Malu 'Aina Center for Non-Violent Education and Action, arrested numerous times for nonviolent direct action including at the Pohakuloa Training Area on the Big Island. Convicted of federal trespass and related charges across multiple actions. Documented in PFOC Breakthrough magazine.

Albertini participated with Jim Douglass and Chuck Giuli in the March 2, 1972 Hickam Air Force Base protest against the Vietnam air war. He and Douglass were convicted of misdemeanor conspiracy and destruction of government property; Giuli’s charges were dismissed. Albertini initially received probation and a $500 fine, then served 90 days for refusing payment. Sources: https://thestreetspirit.org/2015/06/08/street-spirit-interview-with-james-douglass/ ; https://www.ilind.net/2019/07/01/nuremberg-prosecutor-featured-on-60-minutes-defended-hawaii-peace-activists-in-1972-case/ ; https://kyouyou.agu.ac.jp/achievements/file/Journal_204.pdf#page=48
expected_prisoner.body:
Three separately documented 1984 arrests

The original appellate opinion identifies James Vincent Albertini and gives February 4, March 3 and April 7, 1984 as separate Pearl Harbor leafletting arrests. These have separate rows with exact arrest dates. The February count resulted in acquittal in July 1986. The March and April convictions carried suspended prison terms and were reversed on October 15, 1987. Neither suspended punishment nor the reversal establishes actual incarceration or release; those endpoints and durations remain unknown. United States v. Albertini, 830 F.2d 985, original opinion.

Other Hickam and Hilo episodes are not combined with these arrests. Existing identified photograph and the earlier 1972 records are retained. The generic Pohakuloa record still needs independently established custody endpoints.

expected_cases.charges: Federal trespass and related charges — Pohakuloa Training Area and other anti-nuclear protests
expected_cases.sentence: Cumulative federal time across multiple sentences

expected_cases.charges: Conspiracy and destruction of government property — March 2, 1972 Hickam Three action
expected_cases.sentence: March 2, 1972 action at Hickam Air Force Base; FBI arrest followed on March 8. Convicted of misdemeanor conspiracy and destruction of government property. Received one year of probation and a $500 fine. Initial custody duration is not established. The subsequent contempt jail term for refusing payment is recorded separately. Sources: https://www.ilind.net/2019/07/01/nuremberg-prosecutor-featured-on-60-minutes-defended-hawaii-peace-activists-in-1972-case/ ; https://kyouyou.agu.ac.jp/achievements/file/Journal_204.pdf#page=35 ; https://kyouyou.agu.ac.jp/achievements/file/Journal_204.pdf#page=46

expected_cases.charges: Contempt of court — refusal to pay the Hickam Three fine
expected_cases.sentence: Served 90 days in jail in Halawa Valley after refusing the $500 fine; an additional $250 contempt fine was also unpaid. Richard Jeffrey Blair recounts visiting him during imprisonment. Exact admission and release dates are unknown; the documented 90 days are recorded without inventing endpoints. Sources: https://kyouyou.agu.ac.jp/achievements/file/Journal_204.pdf#page=48

attributes.charges: Violation of a Coast Guard security zone — 1984 Hilo Harbor swimming blockade
attributes.sentence: Sentenced to three years in federal prison for the 1984 Hilo Harbor swimming protest against a visiting nuclear warship. In his February 1, 2022 interview, Albertini says he was imprisoned at Terminal Island and later Lompoc, and released after more than a year. Exact arrest day, sentencing date, prison admission and release dates remain unverified; the sentence is not treated as time served. This is separate from the Pearl Harbor leafletting cases and the earlier contempt term. Source: https://couragetoresist.org/podcast-jim-albertini/
